utility.notes: The City of Shasta Lake operates its own municipal electric utility, serving approximately 4,600 retail customers within city limits, confirmed via the city's own Electric Utility page. This is a municipal utility, not PG&E, independently confirmed rather than assumed from county location.

value.name: Shasta Lake Municipal Utility
value.notes: Shasta Lake Municipal Utility is structurally outside CCA enrollment the same way as other municipal utilities in this dataset (Alameda Municipal Power, Gridley Electric Utility, Lompoc Utilities, TDPUD): a CCA only replaces the default generation of an underlying investor-owned utility's (PG&E/SCE/SDG&E) customers, and Shasta Lake's municipal-utility customers are never IOU customers. No CCA operating in Shasta County was found this session. The city's own municipal utility is recorded as both the distribution and generation provider.

permit_authority.value: City of Shasta Lake Electric Department (interconnection), then Development Services Department (building permit)

interconnection_url.notes: As a municipal utility, Shasta Lake's own Electric Department interconnection process applies (NEM A-2 Program), documented on this same Solar page rather than a statewide IOU program.

other_conditions: Original signatures in blue or black ink required on all electric application forms — no digital signatures, e-signatures, or photocopies accepted
Applications including energy storage equipment may require additional review by Shasta Lake Fire Protection District, with additional time and fees

permit_fees.notes: Checked the City's own NEM Program Tariff PDF, Customer-Generator Interconnection Policy PDF, and Electric Rates PDF this session; all three confirm a one-time interconnection application service fee exists but none states its dollar amount (each says the fee 'may be updated by the City from time to time' without listing a current figure). The Electric Rates PDF's Distributed Generation Rate and Net Surplus Compensation Rate are ongoing per-kWh billing rates, not a permit/application fee, so not used here.

rebates.notes: Checked the City's own Efficiency and Rebates page this session; its Residential Rebate Chart covers HVAC, appliances, weatherization, and water conservation, with no solar PV or battery-storage-specific hardware rebate found.
